sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Vijayanagar Dynasties: Tuluva are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Tuluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vira Narasimha Raya founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1505 CE after overthrowing the last ruler of the Saluva dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: During whose reign did the famous Portuguese traveler Domingo Paes visit the Vijayanagara Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveler, visited Vijayanagara around 1520 CE during the reign of Krishnadevaraya and provided a vivid description of the capital city. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Which literary work was written by Krishnadevaraya in Telugu?
practiceQuestions.sol: Amuktamalyada is an epic poem in Telugu composed by Krishnadevaraya. Manucharitramu was written by Allasani Peddana. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the title 'Andhra Bhoja' associated with?
practiceQuestions.sol: Krishnadevaraya held titles like 'Andhra Bhoja', 'Abhinava Bhoja', and 'Murarayara Gaganda' due to his profound patronage of art, literature, and culture. [Primary Reference: NCERT History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous battle of Rakshasa-Tangadi (Talikota) took place in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Battle of Talikota (also known as Rakshasa-Tangadi) was fought on January 23, 1565, leading to the virtual destruction of the Vijayanagara imperial city. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who were the 'Ashtadiggajas' in the court of Krishnadevaraya?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ashtadiggajas were a group of eight exceptionally talented Telugu poets in the royal court of Krishnadevaraya, headed by Allasani Peddana. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q: Which foreign traveler visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya?
practiceQuestions.sol: Fernao Nuniz, a Portuguese horse merchant and chronicler, visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya and wrote a history of the empire. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India Chronicles]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous temple of Vittalaswami at Hampi was built during the reign of which Tuluva ruler?
practiceQuestions.sol: The iconic Vittalaswami temple with its famous stone chariot and musical pillars was initiated and heavily patronized during the reign of Krishnadevaraya. [Primary Reference: An Introduction to Indian Art, NCERT Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the de facto ruler of Vijayanagara during the nominal reign of Sadasiva Raya?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aliya Rama Raya, son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya, held actual political and military power while Sadasiva Raya remained a puppet king under the Tuluva-Aravidu transition. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Sanskrit work on polity was authored by Krishnadevaraya?
practiceQuestions.sol: Krishnadevaraya wrote Sanskrit dramas such as 'Jambavati Kalyanam' and 'Usha Parinayam'. (Note: Amuktamalyada is in Telugu). [Primary Reference: Epigraphical and Literary Canons of Vijayanagara]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the rise of the Tuluva dynasty impact the geopolitical balance of the Deccan Sultanates?
opts: It fostered immediate permanent peace treaties between Vijayanagara and all Deccan Sultanates.
It aggressive military campaigns and decisive victories (such as at Raichur Doab) initially subordinated individual Sultanates before provoking a united coalition.
It led to the complete subjugation and annexation of Bijapur and Golconda into the Vijayanagara core provinces.
It resulted in Vijayanagara completely abandoning its northern frontiers to focus solely on maritime trade.
practiceQuestions.sol: Krishnadevaraya's aggressive policy (‘Yavana-rajya-sthapanacharya’) successfully exploited divisions among the Deccan Sultanates, seizing the Raichur Doab and humbling Bijapur. However, Rama Raya's later interventionist diplomacy alarmed the Sultanates, leading to their unprecedented confederation at Talikota. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Nayankara system during the Tuluva administration?
opts: It was a centralized bureaucratic apparatus where officials received fixed monthly cash salaries from the imperial treasury.
It was a military-feudal assignment system where 'Nayakas' held territory (Amaram) in exchange for maintaining troops and paying regular tribute to the central government.
It was a religious land grant system exclusively meant for Brahmin priests and temple maintenance.
It was a maritime trade guild regulation mechanism overseeing port taxation along the Malabar coast.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nayankara system was crucial to Vijayanagara's military organization. Nayakas controlled land grants called 'Amaram' and were obligated to supply troops and revenue to the central ruler, bolstering Tuluva military might. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Krishnadevaraya manage relations with the Portuguese stationed on the western coast?
opts: By waging continuous holy wars to drive them out of Goa completely.
By maintaining mutually beneficial commercial and diplomatic ties, exchanging trade privileges, horse imports, and military technology.
By forming a total economic embargo and banning all spice exports to Portuguese vessels.
By becoming a direct vassal state of the Portuguese King of Lisbon.
practiceQuestions.sol: Krishnadevaraya maintained pragmatic relations with the Portuguese (such as Albuquerque). He imported prized Arabian horses through Goa and shared common enemies among the Deccan Sultanates, though trade in firearms and horses was closely negotiated. [Primary Reference: Portuguese Chronicles & Vijayanagara History]

practiceQuestions.q: What characterized the architectural evolution during the Tuluva period, particularly under Krishnadevaraya?
opts: Complete rejection of Dravidian architectural canons in favor of pure Nagara style.
Introduction of towering 'Rayagopurams' (monumental gateway towers) and ornate 'Kalyana Mandapas' within temple complexes.
Strict adherence to minimalist structures with zero ornamentation and absence of enclosure walls.
Exclusive use of unbaked mud bricks and timber for all major religious monuments.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tuluva architecture is renowned for towering gateways called 'Rayagopurams', pillared halls, and 'Kalyana Mandapas' (halls for divine marriage ceremonies) carved intricately out of hard stone. [Primary Reference: NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the rule of Krishnadevaraya considered the golden age of Telugu literature?
opts: He banned all regional languages except Sanskrit and Persian.
His personal patronage of the 'Ashtadiggajas' and his own exceptional literary output in Telugu catalyzed an unprecedented creative zenith known as 'Prabandha' literature.
He introduced printing presses from Europe to mass-produce Telugu grammar books.
Telugu was declared the sole official script for all international trade contracts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Krishnadevaraya famously stated 'Desabhashalandu Telugu lessa' (Telugu is the sweetest among regional languages). His court nurtured the Prabandha style of poetry through the Ashtadiggajas. [Primary Reference: Cultural History of Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the provincial administration function under the Tuluva rulers?
opts: The empire was divided into provinces (Rajyas or Mandalam), headed by governors who frequently enjoyed high autonomy and maintained royal-like courts.
Provinces were directly managed by imperial bureaucrats transferred every six months from the capital.
Local self-government village assemblies held complete sovereign powers with no interference from the central ruler.
The empire had no provincial divisions; administration was purely centralized at Hampi.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vijayanagara Empire under the Tuluvas was divided into provinces (Mandalam or Rajya), subdivided into nadu, sthala, and grama. Governors (often royal princes or powerful nobles) enjoyed considerable administrative latitude. [Primary Reference: Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India]

practiceQuestions.q: What economic developments characterized the Tuluva period in Vijayanagara?
opts: Stagnant agrarian output and complete collapse of overseas trade due to internal blockades.
Thriving internal and international trade, construction of massive irrigation tanks, monetization of the economy, and busy ports on both coasts.
A barter-only economic system prohibiting gold and silver coinage.
State monopoly over all agricultural lands with private landownership strictly outlawed.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Tuluva period witnessed robust economic prosperity driven by agriculture (aided by large tanks built by Krishnadevaraya like the Kamalapur tank), extensive trade through ports like Bhatkal and Mangalore, and famous gold coins called Pagodas (Varahas). [Primary Reference: Economic History of Vijayanagara, ASI]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Tuluva rulers approach religious policy and sectarian pluralism?
opts: They enforced a strict religious fundamentalism, persecuting all non-Hindu faiths.
They practiced deep personal devotion to Vaishnavism while maintaining broad tolerance, patronizing Shaivism, Jainism, and extending protection to Muslim merchants and soldiers.
They converted to Islam en masse to appease the surrounding Deccan Sultanates.
They banned temple worship and converted all holy sites into administrative offices.
practiceQuestions.sol: Though personal devotees of Vishnu (Krishnadevaraya was deeply linked to Sri Vaishnavism), Tuluva rulers patronized diverse religious sects, including Shaivism, and employed Muslims in their cavalry, showcasing remarkable pragmatic pluralism. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the strategic importance of the Battle of Raichur (1520) won by Krishnadevaraya?
opts: It secured Vijayanagara's control over the fertile Doab between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, crippling Adil Shah of Bijapur.
It opened a direct land route for Vijayanagara to annex Delhi.
It marked the final permanent peace treaty ending all conflicts with the Bahmani remnants.
It forced the Portuguese to surrender Goa back to the Vijayanagara Empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: The victory at Raichur in 1520 was Krishnadevaraya's crowning military achievement. Capturing the Raichur Doab enhanced Vijayanagara's agricultural wealth, prestige, and dominance over the northern neighbors. [Primary Reference: Robert Sewell, A Forgotten Empire]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the political structure of Vijayanagara change following the Battle of Talikota (1565) under the later Tuluva/Aravidu lineage?
opts: The capital was successfully defended at Hampi and expanded further north.
Hampi was sacked and abandoned, forcing the shifting of the capital eastward to Penukonda and later Chandragiri under the Aravidu dynasty.
The empire dissolved instantly into independent Portuguese colonies.
The Tuluva rulers reconciled with the Sultanates and ruled jointly from Bidar.
practiceQuestions.sol: The devastating defeat at Talikota led to the brutal destruction and depopulation of Hampi. The surviving royal family relocated the capital to Penukonda, marking the definitive decline of imperial grandeur and rise of the Aravidu dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tuluva Dynasty:
1. The dynasty was established by Vira Narasimha Raya in 1505 CE.
2. Krishnadevaraya was the greatest ruler of this dynasty and belonged to the direct lineage of Vira Narasimha Raya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Vira Narasimha Raya founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1505 CE. Statement 2 is incorrect because Krishnadevaraya was the half-brother (or younger brother/relative) of Vira Narasimha Raya, though both were sons of Narasa Nayaka. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 & 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya's literary and cultural contributions:
1. He authored the Telugu classic 'Amuktamalyada' and the Sanskrit drama 'Jambavati Kalyanam'.
2. His court was adorned by the 'Ashtadiggajas', among whom Allasani Peddana was regarded as the grand-father of Telugu poetry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Krishnadevaraya was a prolific scholar who wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Jambavati Kalyanam in Sanskrit. Allasani Peddana, chief among the Ashtadiggajas, held the title 'Andhra-kavitapitamaha'. [Primary Reference: Standard Epigraphical and Literary Sources]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign visitors during the Tuluva dynasty:
1. Domingo Paes visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.
2. Fernao Nuniz recorded historical chronicles during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. Domingo Paes left detailed accounts of Krishnadevaraya's court and Hampi's grandeur around 1520 CE, while Nuniz wrote during Achyuta Deva Raya's reign detailing the history of Vijayanagara kings. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Talikota (1565):
1. It was fought between the united forces of the Deccan Sultanates and the Vijayanagara Empire.
2. Aliya Rama Raya commanded the Vijayanagara army during this battle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. A coalition of four Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, and Bidar) united against Vijayanagara, led in battle by the veteran statesman Aliya Rama Raya. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration and economy under the Tuluva rulers:
1. The 'Nayankara' system was the backbone of provincial military administration.
2. Gold coins minted during this era were commonly known as 'Varahas' or 'Pagodas'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Nayankara system delegated military and revenue authority to local chiefs (Nayakas), and Vijayanagara gold coins (Varahas/Pagodas) circulated widely in international trade. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 & Numismatic Records]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding temple architecture in the Tuluva period:
1. The Hazara Rama temple and Vittalaswami temple are prime examples of Vijayanagara architectural excellence.
2. The construction of massive gateway towers known as 'Gopurams' was discouraged during the Tuluva rule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Hazara Rama and Vittalaswami temples showcase exquisite Tuluva stone carving. Statement 2 is incorrect because massive gateway towers (Rayagopurams) were actively encouraged and became the defining hallmark of Tuluva temple architecture. [Primary Reference: An Introduction to Indian Art, NCERT Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya's military campaigns:
1. He successfully defeated the Gajapati rulers of Odisha and captured Simhadri and Kondapalli.
2. He suffered a severe defeat against the Sultan of Golconda, losing all his southern territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Krishnadevaraya's eastern campaigns against Gajapati Prataparudra of Odisha resulted in the capture of strategic hill forts like Kondapalli and Rajahmundry. Statement 2 is incorrect as Krishnadevaraya was undefeated in his campaigns. [Primary Reference: Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding social conditions and women during the Tuluva period:
1. Women held prominent positions in royal administration, wrestling, astrology, and accountancy.
2. The practice of Sati was entirely unknown and strictly banned across all strata of society.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Foreign travelers like Nuniz and Paes noted that women in Vijayanagara were highly trained in arts, astrology, fencing, and administration. Statement 2 is incorrect because Sati was practiced among the royal and upper classes, as documented by contemporary travelers. [Primary Reference: Foreign Accounts of Vijayanagara, ASI]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the irrigation and public works under Krishnadevaraya:
1. He constructed a large irrigation tank near Kamalapuram with the assistance of Portuguese engineers.
2. He completely neglected agricultural infrastructure, focusing exclusively on expanding standing armies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Domingo Paes described the massive irrigation tank built near Kamalapuram with the aid of Portuguese experts. Statement 2 is incorrect because Krishnadevaraya heavily invested in agricultural waterworks and dams. [Primary Reference: Epigraphical and Archaeological Findings, Hampi]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the succession and decline of the Tuluva Dynasty:
1. Following the death of Krishnadevaraya, Achyuta Deva Raya succeeded him, leading to internal court intrigues.
2. The Tuluva dynasty was succeeded by the Aravidu dynasty after the chaos following the Battle of Talikota and the regency struggles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Achyuta Deva Raya succeeded Krishnadevaraya amidst succession debates involving Saluva Timma's imprisonment and general court factionalism. Ultimately, the Tuluva line faded as the Aravidu dynasty took control under Tirumala Raya after Talikota. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History Textbook]
